title: Access Stamp Service for Residency-Boundary & Retention Audits
creator: Leah Martinez
description: Create an "Access Stamp Service" that produces tamper-evident, time-series snapshots of effective access across tenants tied to data residency tags and retention policies. Each stamp bundle will combine: current RBAC graph, recent SCIM provisioning deltas, active SSO/SAML sessions, and dataset residency labels so auditors can validate who had access to which data at a given point in time. The service will support scheduled snapshots (daily/weekly) and on-demand exports for audits and incident investigations.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Service produces a signed snapshot (JSON + signature) containing: effective roles, resolved permissions, SCIM changelog window, and SSO session metadata for the snapshot window.
2) Snapshots are correlated with dataset residency labels and retention policy identifiers.
3) Export bundles can be retrieved via Console (restricted role) and via secure S3 export for enterprise customers.
4) Snapshots are immutable once stamped and include a checksum and key ID.
5) End-to-end test that simulates role change, SCIM deprovision, and active session shows consistent historical access.
6) Documentation for auditors and runbook for on-call to generate ad-hoc stamps is published.
technical_notes:
- Use current RBAC service (permission-graph) as source of truth; perform a read-only consistent traversal with a snapshot token.
- Consume SCIM change stream (existing reconciler queue) for the last 72h window; include anchored offsets.
- Pull SSO/SAML session logs (login timestamps, session IDs, federated provider) for snapshot interval.
- Tag resources via residency tag service (region, customer-residency-policy) and include tag verifications.
- Stamp signing: use KMS asymmetric key (rotation-aware) to sign bundle manifest; store signature metadata (key id, algorithm) in header.
- Bundles written to hardened storage with retention policy separate from user data retention.
- Provide a compact index for faster query: tenant -> snapshot timestamps -> bundle location.
- Design format to be parity-friendly for auditor ingestion (CSV + normalized JSON views).
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (PoC): read-only RBAC traversal + residency join -> produce unsigned JSON bundle; expose API to request on-demand bundle. (2 sprints)
Phase 2: integrate SCIM offsets and SSO logs; implement KMS signing and immutable write path; smoke tests. (2 sprints)
Phase 3: Console export UX, S3 export for enterprise, access controls for bundle retrieval, audit docs and runbooks. (1 sprint)
Phase 4: Hardening: retention policy for stamps, performance tuning, automated periodic snapshot scheduler with backfill window. (1 sprint)
rollout_plan:
- Internal pilot: enable for staging tenants and compliance team; capture feedback.
- Beta: opt-in for selected enterprise customers with audit requirements.
- GA: enable automatic daily snapshots for tenants on dedicated/enterprise plans; Console and APIs enabled by default for customers that opt into compliance exports.
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for traversal and residency join logic.
- Integration tests: synth tenant with known RBAC/SCIM events -> generate stamp -> verify bundle contents match ground truth.
- Fuzz tests: rapid role flips and SCIM churn to verify snapshot stability.
- Security tests: signature verification flows, KMS key rotation test, access control enforcement for retrieval endpoints.
- Performance: ensure snapshot generation for a 10k-user tenant completes within SLA (target 15 minutes for full snapshot).

2025-02-24: Console export UX prototype demoed to Compliance; feedback: require role-based access to exports and audit trail of who retrieved bundle. Created follow-up ENG ticket to capture retrieval audit. - Leah
2025-02-28: Integration test failing for tenant with >50k principals (memory spike). Mitigating by streaming traversal and chunked bundle writes. Re-estimate remaining work. - Arman
review_feedback: Compliance: prefer daily fixed-time snapshots for high-risk tenants; allow on-demand for incident investigations.
Security: require explicit rotation metadata, and record KMS key usage in audit logs.
Platform: suggest using incremental snapshots + patch bundles for tenants with very large graphs to reduce cost.
Design: produce auditor-friendly CSV exports alongside JSON to simplify review imports.
